source_text:
Ὥστε, ἀδελφοί, ποιοῦντες τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν θεοῦ ἐσόμεθα ἐκ τῆς ἐκκλησίας τῆς πρώτης, τῆς πνευματικῆς, τῆς πρὸ ἡλίου καὶ σελήνης ἐκτισμένης. ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ποιήσωμεν τὸ θέλημα κυρίου, ἐσόμεθα ἐκ τῆς γραφῆς τῆς λεγούσης: Ἐγενήθη ὁ οἶκός μου σπήλαιον λῃστῶν. ὥστε οὖν αἱρετισώμεθα ἀπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας τῆς ζωῆς εἶναι, ἵνα σωθῶμεν.
οὐκ οἴομαι δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, ὅτι ἐκκλησία ζῶσα σῶμά ἐστιν Χριστοῦ: λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφή: Ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς τὸν ἅνθρωπον ἅρσεν καὶ θῆλυ: τὸ ἄρσεν ἐστὶν ὁ Χριστός, τὸ θῆλυ ἡ ἐκκλησία: καὶ ἔτι τὰ βιβλία καὶ οἱ ἀπόστολοι τὴν ἐκκλησίαν οὐ νῦν εἶναι λέγουσιν ἀλλὰ ἄνωθεν. ἦν γὰρ πνευματική, ὡς καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἡμῶν, ἐφανερώθη δὲ ἐπ’ ἐσχάτων τῶν ἡμερῶν, ἵνα ἡμᾶς σώσῃ.
ἡ ἐκκλησία δὲ πνευματικὴ οὖσα ἐφανερώθη ἐν τῇ σαρκὶ Χριστοῦ, δηλοῦσα ἡμῖν, ὅτι ἐάν τις ἡμῶν τηρήσῃ αὐτὴν ἐν τῇ σαρκὶ καὶ μὴ φθείρῃ, ἀπολήψεται αὐτὴν ἐν τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ: ἡ γὰρ σὰρξ αὕτη ἀντίτυπός ἐστιν τοῦ πνεύματος: οὐδεὶς οὖν τὸ ἀντίτυπον φθείρας τὸ αὐθεντικὸν μεταλήψεται. ἄρα οὖν τοῦτο λέγει, ἀδελφοί: τηρήσατε τὴν σάρκα, ἵνα τοῦ πνεύματος μεταλάβητε.
εἰ δὲ λέγομεν εἶναι τὴν σάρκα τὴν ἐκκλησίαν καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα Χριστόν. ἄρα οὖν ὁ ὑβρίσας τὴν σάρκα ὕβρισεν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν. ὁ τοιοῦτος οὖν οὐ μεταλήψεται τοῦ πνεύματος, ὅ ἐστιν ὁ Χριστός.
τοσαύτην δύναται ἡ σὰρξ αὕτη μεταλαβεῖν ζωὴν καὶ ἀφθαρσίαν κολληθέντος αὐτῇ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου, οὔτε ἐξειπεῖν τις δύναται οὔτε λαλῆσαι ἃ ἡτοίμασεν ὁ κύριος τοῖς ἐκλεκτοῖς αὐτοῦ.
thought_title: The Church as the Body of Christ and the Flesh as Its Copy
orientation: The preacher is addressing the congregation as 'brothers,' urging them to do God's will so they belong to the spiritual church that existed before creation, and warning that failure to do God's will makes them the house that became a den of robbers.
pass_a_gloss: So that, brothers, [by] doing the will of our Father God we will be from the church the first, the spiritual, the [one] before sun and moon [that] was created. But if we do not do the will of [the] Lord, we will be from the scripture that says: My house became a cave of robbers. So then let us choose to be from the church of life, so that we may be saved. But I do not think that you are ignorant, that [the] living church is [the] body of Christ: for the scripture says: God made the human male and female: the male is the Christ, the female the church: and still the books and the apostles [say] the church not now to be but from above. For it was spiritual, as also our Jesus, but it was manifested at [the] last of the days, so that he might save us. But the church, being spiritual, was manifested in the flesh of Christ, showing to us, that if anyone of us keeps her in the flesh and does not corrupt [her], he will receive her in the spirit the holy: for this flesh is a copy of the spirit: no one therefore [who] corrupts the copy will share in the original. So then this it says, brothers: keep the flesh, so that you may share in the spirit. But if we say the flesh to be the church and the spirit Christ. So then the [one who] insults the flesh insulted the church. Such a one therefore will not share in the spirit, which is the Christ. So much can this flesh share in life and immortality [when] the spirit the holy has been joined to it, neither can anyone tell nor speak what the Lord prepared for his chosen ones.

choices.term: τῆς πρώτης, τῆς πνευματικῆς, τῆς πρὸ ἡλίου καὶ σελήνης ἐκτισμένης
choices.english: the first church, the spiritual one, which was created before the sun and the moon
choices.why: Keeps the three attributive phrases as a chain modifying 'church,' preserving the emphasis on its pre-cosmic origin and spiritual nature.
rejected: the first, spiritual church created before sun and moon

choices.term: Ἐγενήθη ὁ οἶκός μου σπήλαιον λῃστῶν
choices.english: My house has become a den of robbers
choices.why: Renders the aorist passive 'ἐγενήθη' as 'has become' to convey the completed state, and 'σπήλαιον' as 'den' to match the prophetic imagery of a hideout.
rejected: My house was made a cave of thieves

choices.english: is a copy of the spirit
choices.why: Uses the glossary term 'copy' for ἀντίτυπος, preserving the type-antitype relationship without importing later theological vocabulary.
rejected: is an antitype of the spirit
is a counterpart of the spirit

choices.term: τηρήσατε τὴν σάρκα, ἵνα τοῦ πνεύματος μεταλάβητε
choices.english: keep the flesh, so that you may share in the spirit
choices.why: Keeps the imperative force of 'τηρήσατε' and the purpose clause with 'ἵνα,' preserving the conditional logic of the exhortation.
rejected: guard the flesh in order to receive the spirit

choices.term: κολληθέντος αὐτῇ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου
choices.english: when the Holy Spirit has been joined to it
choices.why: Renders the genitive absolute with 'when' to show the condition under which the flesh can share in life and immortality, and capitalizes 'Holy Spirit' per the glossary.
rejected: the Holy Spirit having been glued to it

choices.term: ἃ ἡτοίμασεν ὁ κύριος τοῖς ἐκλεκτοῖς αὐτοῦ
choices.english: what the Lord has prepared for his chosen ones
choices.why: Keeps the relative clause as the object of 'tell or speak,' preserving the allusion to 1 Corinthians 2:9 without naming it.
rejected: the things which the Lord prepared for his elect

pass_b_english: So then, brothers and sisters, if we do the will of God our Father, we will belong to the first church, the spiritual church, the church created before the sun and the moon. But if we do not do the will of the Lord, we will belong to what the scripture says: "My house has become a den of robbers" (Jeremiah 7:11). Let us therefore choose to belong to the church of life, so that we may be saved.

I do not think you are unaware that the living church is the body of Christ. For the scripture says, "God made the human being male and female" (Genesis 1:27). The male is Christ, and the female is the church. And further, the books of the prophets and the apostles say that the church is not from now but from above. For the church was spiritual, as was our Jesus, but it was revealed in the last days so that it might save us.

The church, being spiritual, was revealed in the flesh of Christ, and in this it shows us that if any of us guards the church in his own flesh and does not corrupt it, he will receive the church back in the Holy Spirit. For this flesh is a copy of the spirit. No one, then, who corrupts the copy will share in the original. This, then, is what it means, brothers and sisters: keep the flesh pure, so that you may share in the spirit.

But if we say that the flesh is the church and the spirit is Christ, then the one who has insulted the flesh has insulted the church. Such a person, then, will not share in the spirit, which is Christ.
This flesh can share in such great life and immortality when the Holy Spirit has been joined to it, that no one can declare or speak what the Lord has prepared for his chosen ones.

last_rejected.source_quote: Ἐγενήθη ὁ οἶκός μου σπήλαιον λῃστῶν
last_rejected.why: The citation is wrong; this is Matthew 21:13/Mark 11:17/Luke 19:46 quoting Jeremiah 7:11, but in this context it's a NT allusion, not directly Jeremiah.
last_rejected.fix: Remove the parenthetical citation or correct to Matthew 21:13.
last_rejected.ruling: The quote matches Jeremiah 7:11 LXX; citing Jeremiah is defensible and within normal scholarly range, not a clear major error.

last_rejected.why: The antecedent of 'it' is unclear; 'he will receive her' (the church) is meant, but 'it' obscures that the church is received.
last_rejected.ruling: αὐτήν is feminine; 'it' referring to ἐκκλησία is standard English. Not a meaning-changing mistranslation.

problems.why: Inconsistent address to same audience; reader may think different groups are meant.

problems.quote: No one, then, who corrupts the copy will share in the original
problems.why: 'Copy' and 'original' need antecedents; reader cannot tell what is being corrupted.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'who corrupts the flesh, which is a copy of the spirit.'

problems.quote: no one can tell out or speak what the Lord has prepared
problems.why: 'Tell out' is not standard English; likely means 'declare' or 'recount.'

edits.old: So then, brothers, if we do the will
edits.new: So then, brothers and sisters, if we do the will

edits.old: This, then, is what it says, brothers: keep the flesh
edits.new: This, then, is what it says, brothers and sisters: keep the flesh

edits.old: No one, then, who corrupts the copy will share in the original.
edits.new: No one, then, who corrupts the flesh, which is a copy of the spirit, will share in the original.

edits.old: no one can tell out or speak what the Lord has prepared
edits.new: no one can declare or speak what the Lord has prepared

fixed: The address 'brothers' was standardized to 'brothers and sisters' in the two places where it occurred in the English.
The copy/original sentence was clarified by adding the antecedent 'the flesh, which is a copy of the spirit.'
'Tell out' was replaced with 'declare' as suggested.

problems.why: Same audience addressed three different ways; reader may wonder if 'my brothers' signals a different subgroup.

problems.quote: But if we say that the flesh is the church and the spirit is Christ, then the one who has insulted the flesh has insulted the church.
problems.why: The logic is compressed and confusing: the analogy shifts between flesh/spirit and church/Christ without clear transitions.
problems.fix: Expand the analogy: 'if the flesh corresponds to the church and the spirit to Christ...'

edits.old: But if we say that the flesh is the church and the spirit is Christ, then the one who has insulted the flesh has insulted the church.
edits.new: But if we say that the flesh corresponds to the church and the spirit to Christ, then the one who has insulted the flesh has insulted the church.

fixed: The 'brothers and sisters' problem is a style demand, not a source misstatement; the English already uses 'brothers and sisters' consistently in this section, so no edit is needed.

The logic is compressed in the source too (εἰ δὲ λέγομεν εἶναι τὴν σάρκα τὴν ἐκκλησίαν καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα Χριστόν), but the English can clarify the correspondence without changing meaning; edited to 'corresponds to'.

problems.why: Reader may wonder if 'brothers' and 'brothers and sisters' address different groups.
problems.fix: Use one form consistently or note that 'brothers' is inclusive.

edits.old: So then, brothers and sisters, if we do the will
edits.new: So then, brothers, if we do the will

edits.old: This, then, is what it says, brothers and sisters: keep the flesh
edits.new: This, then, is what it says, brothers: keep the flesh

fixed: The source uses ἀδελφοί ('brothers'), which the brief's glossary does not require to be rendered as 'brothers and sisters.' The earlier edits introduced inconsistency; reverting to 'brothers' throughout restores consistency with the source and the brief.

polish.changed: Clarified pronoun references and subject shifts, made the argument about the church, flesh, and spirit easier to follow, and smoothed sentence rhythm for reading aloud.
Clarified the address to the congregation, explained the reference to the Old Testament books and the apostles, and smoothed the sentence flow while preserving every claim and quotation.

notes.why: The congregation is addressed with three different forms; a reader may wonder if different groups or tones are intended.
notes.fix: Standardize to one form throughout, or note that all forms address the same congregation.

notes.why: This phrase refers to the Old Testament ('the books') and New Testament/apostolic writings, but a modern reader may not catch the distinction.
notes.fix: Note that 'the books' = Scripture and 'the apostles' = apostolic writings.

notes.quote: the first church, the spiritual one, the church created before the sun and the moon
notes.why: The concept of a pre-existent, spiritual church is not explained; a modern reader may confuse it with the earthly congregation.
notes.fix: Note this refers to a heavenly, pre-existent Church, a concept found in early Christian theology.

polish.changed: Clarified the church-flesh-spirit analogy by naming what is guarded and received, replaced the vague 'books of the Old Testament' with 'books of the prophets,' and smoothed sentence flow for reading aloud.

notes.quote: the books of the Old Testament and the apostles
notes.why: Vague reference; reader cannot identify which specific books are meant.
notes.fix: Note this refers generally to Scripture and apostolic writings.

notes.quote: if any of us keeps the church in the flesh and does not corrupt it, he will receive it in the Holy Spirit
notes.why: 'Keeps the church in the flesh' is opaque; the analogy between flesh/church/spirit is hard to follow.
notes.fix: Clarify: 'keeps his flesh pure as the church's copy.'
